finding.sequence_description: I2: Control vs attack for token freshness. First obtain a valid access token via password grant, then attempt to use the same user credentials after disabling the user (config change) to ensure new tokens cannot be minted. This tests whether Keycloak incorrectly allows token issuance for a disabled principal (freshness/validity of credential artifacts after administrative invalidation).
finding.description: [LLM-Judge] Test could not evaluate token freshness/disabled-user behavior because the OIDC client was never created (client creation failed), causing all password-grant attempts to fail with invalid_client.

sequence.description: I2: Control vs attack for token freshness. First obtain a valid access token via password grant, then attempt to use the same user credentials after disabling the user (config change) to ensure new tokens cannot be minted. This tests whether Keycloak incorrectly allows token issuance for a disabled principal (freshness/validity of credential artifacts after administrative invalidation).
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I2: After an administrative invalidation (user disabled), subsequent token minting using the same credentials must be rejected; previously issued tokens may remain valid until expiry, but new artifacts must not be issued.

finding.sequence_description: I4 attack: Empty-sub / missing-sub confusion via OIDC request object. Attempt to get two distinct authorization requests to map to the same downstream subject due to empty or missing subject-like identifiers being treated as a default/anonymous principal.
